title: The manifest, JCS and pinning
source: spec/socket-draft-00.md (doc rev 39), spec/ERRATA.md, spec/DECISIONS.md, registry/generated/registry.json, reference/python/bnap_ref.py
header: The manifest is JSON at /.well-known/bnap, signed by its root key over
H_bnap/manifest(JCS(manifest without sig)) (draft-00 9.1). Manifests are given as the exact
bytes in hex. JCS assumes I-JSON (RFC 7493), so duplicate member names, non-integer numbers,
integers beyond 2^53, null and lone surrogates are refused: two parsers must never read two
documents out of one signed byte string. Root key SHA-256("bnap test root key"), backup
SHA-256("bnap test backup key"), as in vectors.json.

Valid.description: A well-formed input every implementation must accept.

Signature.description: sig does not verify under root.

Time.description: issued, max_age and the client's clock disagree beyond 60 s.

Skew.description: At the edge of the 60 s skew.

DuplicateMember.description: Two members with one name: a parser differential on signed JSON.

IJson.description: A value I-JSON and 9.1 do not allow.

Rollback.description: A lower seq, or the same seq with other bytes.

Rotation.description: A root rotation signed by the pinned backup.

Stolen.description: The current root tries to replace the backup.

DoubleRotation.description: A client that missed one rotation sees a second.

Lapse.description: The pin lapsed, so the client trusts on first use again.

Native.description: A native challenge the 9.3 rules forbid paying.
